## Overview

This case study evaluated the energy and water performance of Ellison Hall, a high-occupancy academic building at UCSB originally built in 1969. Despite earning LEED Gold certification, Ellison Hall revealed ongoing inefficiencies, particularly in water use, that could be addressed through cost-effective retrofits. The assessment focused on ENERGY STAR benchmarking, indoor water use analysis, and recommendations for both low-cost and capital-intensive improvements to align the building with UCSB’s climate action goals.

## Use of R Studio

This project also allowed me to apply skills gained in my Environmental Data Science coursework. Although data analysis was not explicitly required for this case study, I took the initiative to organize, clean, and visualize the utility data collected for Ellison Hall. For instance, water and electricity usage data for the building did not follow the standard calendar year, requiring careful data wrangling to ensure it could be plotted effectively. This process included converting electricity and natural gas usage to a common unit (kBtu) and restructuring the data for accurate visualization.

Adding customized figures and visualizations to this project not only showcased my technical skills but also deepened my understanding of how to present data with intention. As shown in the figures below, I wrote code to compare Ellison Hall's water and energy use intensity (EUI) to baseline metrics and national averages. This work highlights my ability to critically assess data, apply coding skills to real-world scenarios, and present findings in a clear and impactful way.

## Code

```{r warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}

# reading in packages 
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)

# reading in data
green <- read.csv("data/GB.csv")
utility <- read.csv("data/Utilitydata.csv")

```

```{r}

# creating a new data frame and selecting on necessary rows
green_clean <- green |> 
  filter(Location %in% c("Ellison", "National"))


# EUI Data Visual 
ggplot(data = green_clean,
       aes(x = Location,
           y = EUI,
           fill = Location)) +
  
  geom_col() +
  
  geom_text(aes(label = round(EUI, 1)),  
            vjust = -0.5,                
            size = 2.5) + 
  
  labs(title = "Ellison Hall Energy Use Intensity Compared to the National Average ",
       x = "Site Location",
       y = "Energy Use Intensity (kBtu/ft²)") +
  
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Ellison" = "blue4",
                     "National" = "red4")) +
  
  theme_bw() + 
  
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 10),
        panel.grid.major = element_line(color = NA),
        panel.grid.minor = element_line(color = NA),
        legend.position = "none")
  
```

```{r}

# change the order of the bar chart to keep it consistent
green$Location <- factor(green$Location, levels = c("Ellison", "Baseline"))

```

```{r}

# to make sure the csv file is read is as a number and no separate values are separated by commas 
green$Water <- as.numeric(gsub(",", "", green$Water))

# creating new data frame with only necessary rows
green_water <- green |> 
  filter(Location %in% c("Ellison", "Baseline"))

# Water Visual
ggplot(data = green_water,
       aes(x = Location,
           y = Water,
           fill = Location)) +
  
  geom_col() +
  
  geom_text(aes(label = round(Water, 1)),  
            vjust = -0.5,                
            size = 2.5) +
  
  labs(title = "Ellison Hall Annual Water Consumption Compared to the Baseline ",
       x = "Location",
       y = "Water Consumption (gallons)") +
  
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Ellison" = "blue4",
                     "Baseline" = "red4")) +
  
  theme_bw() + 
  
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 10),
        panel.grid.major = element_line(color = NA),
         panel.grid.minor = element_line(color = NA),
        legend.position = "none")


```

```{r}

# converting values into a common unit (kBtu)
utility_clean <- utility |> 
  clean_names() |> 
  mutate(
    electric_meter_usage = as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.]", "", electric_meter_usage)) * 3.412,
    gas_meter_usage = as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.]", "", gas_meter_usage)) * 1.037) |> 

  mutate(date = as_factor(date),
         date = fct_relevel(date, 
                            "7/1", "8/1", "9/1", "10/1", "11/1", "12/1", "1/1", "2/1", "3/1", "4/1", "5/1", "6/1")) |> 


  select(date, electric_meter_usage, gas_meter_usage) |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = c(electric_meter_usage, gas_meter_usage),
               names_to = "meter_type",
               values_to = "usage_kbtu")

```

```{r}

# Electric vs. Natural Gas usage Visual
ggplot(data = utility_clean,
       aes(x = date,
           y = usage_kbtu,
           color = meter_type,
           group = meter_type)) +
  
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  
  scale_color_manual(values = c("electric_meter_usage" = "yellow1", "gas_meter_usage" = "darkorchid3"),
                      labels = c("Electric Grid", "Natural Gas")) +
  
  labs(title = "Ellison Hall's Energy Use by Calender Month (2021-2022)",
       x = "",
       y = "Site Energy (kBtu)", # cleaning the title names
      color = "") + 
  
  theme_bw() +

 theme(
  panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white"), # changing the background color
  plot.title = element_text(size = 9),
  panel.grid.major = element_line(color = NA), # removing the color to the grid lines
  panel.grid.minor = element_line(color = NA), # removing the color to the grid lines
  axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
  axis.title.x = element_text(size = 8),  # this is correct
  axis.title.y = element_text(size = 8)   # adjust if needed
)


```
